links.comparator_used: Same radiologists reading chest radiographs without AI-generated reports
links.outcome: Accuracy for TB-related abnormality detection and localization performance with vs without AI-generated reports
links.effect: Accuracy reader 1: 93.4% without vs 94.1% with AI reports (p=.47); reader 2: 91.3% without vs 93.5% with (p=.03). Localization reader 1: 79.8% vs 78.7% (p=.71); reader 2: 77.9% vs 81.5% (p=.23).
links.tradeoff: Radiologists accepted few AI reports for abnormal radiographs without modification (reader 1: 52.4%; reader 2: 37.0%), versus 91.7% and 83.2% for normal radiographs, so abnormal cases still need substantial editing.
links.quote: Accuracy was significantly lower for AI-generated reports than for both readers alone (p < .001), but significantly higher with than without AI-generated reports for one reader (reader 1: p = .47; reader 2: p = .03).

links.comparator_used: Standalone AI-generated reports without radiologist review
links.outcome: Accuracy and localization of TB-related abnormality detection, AI alone vs radiologists using AI reports
links.effect: Standalone AI accuracy 90.8% (sensitivity 95.2%, specificity 86.7%) vs 94.1% for reader 1 and 93.5% for reader 2 with AI reports. Standalone AI localization 63.3% vs 78.7% and 81.5% for readers with AI reports.
links.quote: Although AI-generated reports may augment radiologists' diagnostic assessments, the current model requires human oversight, given inferior standalone performance.
